summary: The PR lookup matches open PRs by unqualified head branch name and reuses the first match, so a same-named fork PR can be recorded as the run's PR; the rest of the diff has no injection, secret or permission defect.

findings.summary: Step 9 item 3.1 reuses the first open PR matching the bare head branch name without limiting it to this repository or the default base, and item 3.4 reads assignees from whatever PR the lookup returns, so a foreign fork PR can be recorded as the run's published PR and checked in its place.
findings.evidence: SKILL.md:159 reads 'Branch PR lookup: `gh pr list --head <branch> --state open --json url,assignees`. Exit 0 with entries: found; reuse the first entry's `url` and skip creation.' No --base and no isCrossRepository or headRepositoryOwner filter is given. `gh pr list --help` documents `-H, --head string  Filter by head branch ("<owner>:<branch>" syntax not supported)`, so the filter is by branch name alone and the same name can match PRs from any fork. The field list from `gh pr list --help` includes isCrossRepository and headRepositoryOwner. SKILL.md:162 (item 3.4) says 'Found: use its assignees for item 4' without selecting the entry whose url equals the URL `gh pr create` printed, so with several matches the assignment check can read another PR's assignees. Item 4 (SKILL.md:163) then calls set-status pr-open with that URL. tools/tests/test_pr_publication.py checks only the literal lookup string and cannot detect this. Rules: ENG-25, ENG-26. Confidence: code path demonstrated by reading the text; GitHub-side fork matching inferred from gh's help text, not run against live GitHub.
findings.fix: Scope the lookup to this repository's default base and same-repository heads: `gh pr list --head <branch> --base <default-branch> --state open --json url,assignees,isCrossRepository`. Reuse only entries with isCrossRepository false. In item 3.4 and item 4, take the assignees from the entry whose url equals the URL printed by `gh pr create`, and treat no exact match as an assignment problem. Update the text-contract test with an element that fails when the base scope or the same-repository filter is removed, and add a matching injected-failure case.
